sources.title: HSE's Planning Advice Web App
sources.role: Official land-use-planning advice service for major hazard sites and pipelines.
sources.facts: The app uses inner, middle and outer consultation zones plus development type, size and intensity to return HSE advice.
sources.guard: A web-app result is planning advice, not planning permission, hazardous-substances consent, a site safety certificate or proof that all hazards are captured.

sources.title: HSE's land use planning methodology
sources.role: Official methodology for statutory-consultee advice near major hazards.
sources.facts: The methodology combines consultation zones, development sensitivity levels and decision rules to produce Advises Against or Does Not Advise Against advice.
sources.guard: Methodology and mapped zones do not prove exact development geometry, current plant inventory, risk acceptability or the planning authority's final decision.

sources.title: What is HSE's role?
sources.role: Official explanation of HSE's planning advisory role.
sources.facts: HSE is a statutory consultee for relevant applications around major hazard sites and major accident hazard pipelines.
sources.guard: Statutory-consultee status does not prove that consultation occurred, that HSE supports a proposal or that permission was granted.

sources.title: Developers' planning application advice
sources.role: Official pre-application route for sites near major hazards.
sources.facts: Developers can check whether a site lies within an HSE consultation zone and seek an indication of HSE advice.
sources.guard: Pre-application advice is not a final consultation response, planning permission, safety case, consent or construction approval.

sources.title: Land use planning (LUP) – public safety advice
sources.role: Official collection for land-use planning, hazardous-substances consent and public-safety advice.
sources.facts: The collection separates major-hazard planning advice, hazardous-substances consent, fire-safety planning and EIA consultation routes.
sources.guard: A collection page does not establish which route applies to a particular parcel or whether any application has been submitted or decided.

sources.title: Introduction to Control of Major Accident Hazards (COMAH)
sources.role: Official introduction to COMAH 2015 and competent-authority functions.
sources.facts: COMAH requires businesses to take measures to prevent major accidents involving dangerous substances and limit consequences.
sources.guard: COMAH scope or operator duties do not prove a particular establishment is compliant, accident-free, suitable for nearby development or currently operational.

sources.title: Control Of Major Accident Hazards Regulations 2015 (COMAH)
sources.facts: COMAH aims to prevent and mitigate major accidents and includes public-information and emergency-planning duties.
sources.guard: Regulatory guidance does not replace establishment-specific safety reports, inspections, emergency plans, enforcement records or planning consultation.

sources.title: Public information on establishments subject to COMAH 2015
sources.role: Official public-information search route for operational COMAH establishments.
sources.facts: Published information describes establishments in scope because dangerous substances are present at or above qualifying thresholds.
sources.guard: Public records may be search-specific and do not prove complete site boundaries, current quantities, exact consultation zones, compliance or absence of unlisted hazards.

package_guard: Hazard-planning advice, consultation zones, COMAH records and regulatory guidance do not by themselves prove exact-site hazard exposure, current inventories, safety, consent, permission, mitigation, insurability, funding or deliverability.
